- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) and recent history shows downward momentum.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent high sentiment; cap growth to avoid overshoot.
- Allow slight downward bias in forecasts when sentiment is mixed or declining, especially after recent peaks.
- Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment if sentiment is volatile or inconsistent over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is >0.8 and forecast is >10% above recent 14-day high, apply downward adjustment of 5–15% to avoid overconfidence bias.
